title: Modibo Keïta Elected to French National Assembly
note: Keita was elected to the French National Assembly in 1956, not 1952. In 1952 he was re-elected to the territorial assembly of French Sudan.

title: Loi Cadre Grants French Sudan Internal Self-Government
note: Loi Cadre passed June 23, 1956. Correct year and substance confirmed.

title: Mali Federation Formed Between French Sudan and Senegal
note: Federation founded April 4, 1959. Keita as president, Senghor led political bureau — confirmed.

title: Mali Achieves Independence — Federation Then Dissolves
note: Federation independent June 20, 1960; Senegal withdrew August 1960; Republic of Mali declared September 22, 1960 — all confirmed.

title: Mali Withdraws from CFA Franc Zone
note: Mali withdrew from the CFA franc zone on July 1, 1962, not 1961. Franco-Malian monetary agreement was March 9, 1962; Mali franc introduced July 1, 1962.

title: First Tuareg Rebellion Against the Malian State
note: Rebellion began 1962–1964 in Adrar des Ifoghas. Suppressed with Algerian and Moroccan assistance — confirmed.

title: Nationalization of Trade and Socialist Economic Model
note: Keita nationalized wholesale trade and expelled French and Lebanese firms as part of his African socialist program — confirmed.

title: Mali Returns to Franc Zone Under IMF Austerity
note: Mali signed monetary agreement returning to franc zone circa 1967, with IMF austerity conditions — confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Military Coup Overthrows Keïta — Traoré Takes Power
note: Coup November 19, 1968, led by Lt. Moussa Traoré. Keita died in detention 1977 — confirmed.

title: Great Sahel Famine Kills Hundreds of Thousands
note: 1973 peak of Sahel famine confirmed; Mali among hardest-hit. Death tolls and affected regions match.

title: New Constitution Formalizes One-Party Rule Under UDPM
note: Constitution adopted by referendum June 2, 1974; formalized UDPM one-party rule — confirmed.

title: IMF Structural Adjustment Program Imposed
note: Mali entered IMF structural adjustment programs in the early 1980s with austerity conditions — broadly confirmed, specific 1980 date is approximate.

title: Tuareg Veterans Join Gadhafi's Islamic Legion in Libya
note: Tuareg recruitment into the Islamic Legion is confirmed but began in the 1970s, not specifically 1984. The year 1984 is not corroborated; recruitment was an ongoing process through the 1970s–80s.

title: Border War with Burkina Faso Over Agacher Strip
note: Christmas War December 25–30, 1985; ICJ ruled December 22, 1986 splitting the territory — confirmed.

title: Democracy Movement Emerges in Mali
note: AEEM student movement and pro-democracy activism emerged in late 1980s–1989 — confirmed.

title: Second Tuareg Rebellion — Libya Veterans Return Armed
note: MPA attacked Ménaka/Tidarmène June 28–29, 1990; Libyan legion veterans confirmed as fighters — confirmed.

title: March Massacre — Security Forces Kill Pro-Democracy Protesters
note: March 22, 1991 massacre; death toll estimates 150–300 — confirmed. Description of 100–300 range is consistent with sources.

title: Coup Ends Traoré Era — ATT Launches Democratic Transition
note: Coup March 26, 1991, by Lt. Col. ATT; National Conference followed — confirmed.

title: National Conference Charts Path to Multi-Party Democracy
note: National Conference July–August 1991; adopted new constitution and electoral code — confirmed.

title: Alpha Oumar Konaré Elected First Democratic President
note: Konaré won April 1992 election with ~69% second-round vote — confirmed. Event description says 77% which is incorrect; 77.6% was IBK in 2013, not Konaré.

title: National Pact Ends Second Tuareg Rebellion
note: National Pact signed April 11, 1992 in Bamako with Algerian mediation — confirmed.

title: Commercial Gold Mining Begins — Economic Transformation
note: Syama mine was developed by BHP in the 1980s; industrial gold production grew from 1993 but the specific 1993 commercial start date for Syama is not confirmed by sources.

title: Flame of Peace Ceremony Ends Second Tuareg Rebellion
note: Flame of Peace ceremony March 27, 1996 in Timbuktu; over 3,000 weapons destroyed — confirmed.

title: Decentralization Reform Creates Elected Local Communes
note: Urban commune elections held 1998; rural commune elections 1999. The reform framework was finalized 1996–98 — confirmed.

title: HIPC Debt Relief Frees Resources for Development
note: Mali reached HIPC decision point September 2000; ~$675 million in debt relief — confirmed.

title: Amadou Toumani Touré Elected President Democratically
note: ATT won 2002 election as independent with 65% second-round vote; inaugurated June 8, 2002 — confirmed.

title: GSPC Hostage Crisis Reveals Northern Mali as Jihadist Sanctuary
note: 32 European tourists kidnapped; hostages moved to Mali; released August 18, 2003 for €5 million ransom — confirmed.

title: Third Tuareg Rebellion — Ag Bahanga Attacks Northern Bases
note: ADC attacks on Kidal/Ménaka bases May 23, 2006; Algiers accord July 2006; Bahanga refused to sign — confirmed.

title: AQIM Kidnappings and Ransom Operations Escalate
note: AQIM kidnapping operations in Sahel using northern Mali as hub confirmed as escalating in 2007 onward.

title: Gadhafi's Fall Returns Armed Tuareg Fighters to Mali
note: Gaddafi death October 2011; Tuareg fighters with looted Libyan weapons returned to Mali — confirmed.

title: Military Coup Overthrows ATT Government
note: Coup March 22, 2012 by Captain Amadou Sanogo — confirmed.

title: MNLA and Islamists Seize Northern Mali — Azawad Declared
note: Kidal/Gao fell March, Timbuktu April 1; Azawad independence declared April 6, 2012 — confirmed.

title: Islamists Impose Sharia and Destroy Timbuktu Heritage Sites
note: Ansar Dine imposed sharia; 14 of 16 UNESCO mausoleums destroyed from June 30, 2012; ICC conviction followed — confirmed.

title: ECOWAS Sanctions and Transitional Government Installed
note: ECOWAS sanctions and Dioncounda Traoré installed as interim president under pressure — confirmed.

title: Operation Serval — France Repels Islamist Advance
note: Launched January 11, 2013 after Konna fell January 10; rapid liberation of northern cities — confirmed.

title: MINUSMA UN Peacekeeping Mission Deployed
note: MINUSMA deployed July 1, 2013; became deadliest UN peacekeeping mission — confirmed.

title: Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta Elected President
note: IBK won August 11, 2013 second round with 77.6% — confirmed.

title: Operation Barkhane Replaces Serval — Permanent French Presence
note: Barkhane launched August 1, 2014; ~3,000 troops (not 5,000 as stated) across five Sahel states — VERIFIED with minor size discrepancy.

title: Algiers Peace Agreement Signed with Northern Armed Groups
note: Agreement signed May 15 and June 20, 2015 in Bamako after negotiations in Algiers — confirmed.

title: Radisson Blu Hotel Attack Brings Jihad to Bamako
note: Attack November 20, 2015; 170 hostages taken; 20 killed (not 22) — VERIFIED with minor casualty discrepancy.

title: JNIM Forms — Sahel Jihadist Groups Unify Under AQIM
note: JNIM announced March 2, 2017; Ansar Dine, AQIM Sahara Emirate, Macina Liberation Front, al-Mourabitoun merged under Iyad Ag Ghaly — confirmed.

title: Ogossagou Massacre — Over 160 Fulani Civilians Killed
note: March 23, 2019; ~160 Fulani killed in Mopti region by Dogon hunters; government PM resigned — confirmed.

title: Mass Protests and M5-RFP Coalition Demand IBK's Resignation
note: M5-RFP protests from June 5, 2020 demanding IBK resignation over corruption and security failures — confirmed.

title: Military Coup Removes IBK — Goïta's Junta Takes Power
note: Coup August 18, 2020; IBK arrested and resigned on live television — confirmed.

title: Second Coup by Goïta Installs Full Military Control
note: May 24, 2021; Goïta arrested Bah N'Daw and Ouane over cabinet reshuffle; constitutional court named Goïta transitional president — confirmed.

title: Wagner Group Mercenaries Deployed in Mali
note: Wagner deployment began December 2021; hundreds of mercenaries confirmed — confirmed.

title: France Ends Operation Barkhane — Troops Withdrawn from Mali
note: Last French troops withdrew August 15, 2022; Barkhane formally ended November 9, 2022 — confirmed.

title: Moura Massacre — Wagner and Malian Forces Kill 500 Civilians
note: March 27–31, 2022; UN concluded 500+ unlawfully killed; HRW said 300+; predominantly Fulani men — confirmed.

title: Junta Expels MINUSMA — UN Peacekeeping Mission Ends
note: Junta requested withdrawal June 16, 2023; Security Council terminated mandate June 30; withdrawal completed December 31, 2023 — confirmed.

title: Alliance des États du Sahel Formed — Mali Pivots from ECOWAS
note: Liptako-Gourma charter signed September 16, 2023; mutual defense pact between Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger — confirmed.

title: Mali Formally Withdraws from ECOWAS
note: Withdrawal announced January 28, 2024; formally took effect January 29, 2025 after one-year ECOWAS treaty notice period — confirmed. Year coded as 2024 (announcement) is accurate.

title: Junta Indefinitely Postpones Elections — Military Rule Entrenched
note: Elections indefinitely postponed; Goïta secured five-year presidential mandate via military-appointed parliament July 2025; political parties dissolved May 2025 — confirmed.
